facts.statement: The genus Batrachotomus was formally described by paleontologist David J. Gower twenty-two years after the initial discovery of its fossils.
facts.quote: Batrachotomus was described by palaeontologist David J. Gower 22 years after its discovery.

facts.statement: Unlike sprawling reptiles such as crocodiles, Batrachotomus possessed an erect stance that gave it locomotor superiority and agility.
facts.quote: In contrast with sprawling reptiles, like crocodiles, this large carnivore was very agile with locomotor superiority due to its erect stance.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Batrachotomus, identified as SMNS 52970, preserves a femur measuring 47.8 cm and a skull approximately 50 cm long.
facts.quote: The holotype and largest known specimen (SMNS 52970), composed of an almost complete skull and partial postcranial skeleton, preserves a 47.8 cm long femur, and a ~50 cm long skull.

facts.statement: The paired bony plates on Batrachotomus's back are scientifically known as osteoderms.
facts.quote: These bony deposits forming scales are called osteoderms.

facts.statement: Batrachotomus exhibited heterodonty, possessing sharp teeth that were laterally compressed and varied in size and shape.
facts.quote: The jaws contained sharp teeth which were compressed laterally and unequal in size and shape, and this variation of tooth shape is known as heterodonty.

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Batrachotomus held 30 teeth distributed across the premaxillae and maxillae, while the lower jaw contained 22 teeth.
facts.quote: The upper jaw bore 30 teeth, with each premaxilla carrying about 4 teeth and each maxilla 11, while the lower jaw held 22 teeth.

facts.statement: The first specimens of Batrachotomus were discovered by fossil collector Johann G. Wegele during a 1977 excavation at the Erfurt Formation.
facts.quote: Fossil collector Johann G. Wegele discovered the first specimens in a 1977 excavation at the Erfurt Formation, dated from the Longobardian (late Ladinian) age.

facts.statement: Fossils of Batrachotomus remained undescribed until 1999, at which point they were previously referred to by paleontologists as "Kupferzellia" or simply "rauisuchid".
facts.quote: The fossils recovered from a marlstone remained undescribed until 1999 and palaeontologists referred to the genus simply as "rauisuchid" or "Kupferzellia".

facts.statement: Batrachotomus lived in southern Germany during the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic, approximately 242 to 237 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils of this animal have been found in southern Germany and dated from the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic period, around 242 to 237 million years ago.

facts.statement: Batrachotomus inhabited a swampy region in southern Germany.
facts.quote: The locality where Batrachotomus lived was a swampy region

facts.statement: The name Batrachotomus translates to "frog cutter" in Greek, referencing its predation on the large amphibian Mastodonsaurus.
facts.quote: the name comes from the Greek batrachos/βάτραχος (frog) and tome/τομή (cutting, slicing), which refers to its preying on the large amphibian Mastodonsaurus.

facts.statement: The ecosystem where Batrachotomus lived included diverse fauna such as fishes, amphibians like Gerrothorax and Mastodonsaurus, nothosaurs, and the marine reptile Tanystropheus.
facts.quote: Along with Batrachotomus, palaeontologists recovered remains of fishes, amphibians, such as Gerrothorax and Mastodonsaurus, and even animals like nothosaurs and the distinct marine reptile Tanystropheus.

facts.statement: A 2011 revision by Sterling J. Nesbitt suggested that the family Prestosuchidae is non-monophyletic based on comprehensive phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: Sterling J. Nesbitt (2011) revised the classification of basal archosaurs, and using the most comprehensive phylogenetic analysis for this group (to date) found Prestosuchidae to be non-monophyletic.

facts.statement: Recent analyses classify Batrachotomus as a basal loricatan that is most closely related to the clades containing Crocodylomorpha and Rauisuchidae.
facts.quote: The members of this clade were recovered as basal loricatan, of which Batrachotomus was found to be the most derived i.e. most closely related to the clade containing Crocodylomorpha and Rauisuchidae.

facts.statement: The time range for Batrachotomus is recorded as the Ladinian stage, specifically between 239.48 and 237 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ladinian to Ladinian (239.48 to 237 million years ago)

facts.statement: It was hypothesized by Michael Parrish that Batrachotomus originally belonged to the family Rauisuchidae, though later analyses placed it in Prestosuchidae.
facts.quote: Parrish hypothesized that Batrachotomus (then "Kupferzellia") belonged to the family of Rauisuchidae, another clade of carnivorous reptiles, and species of Rauisuchus.

rejected.statement: A distinctive feature of Batrachotomus was a row of paired, flattened bony plates running along its back.
rejected.quote: A remarkable feature seen on its back was a row of paired, flattened bony plates.
